title: Quantile-derivative token-rate harness for drift-sensitive TPS monitoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a microbenchmark harness that measures tokens/sec across core serving variants using quantile-derivative analysis to detect subtle regressions in tail performance (p95/p99). The harness should produce stable canary runs, support automated bisect inputs, and emit artifacts for dashboards and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Daily canary job produces a reproducible tokens/sec profile for configured model/hardware pairs and stores artifacts to s3://rio-benchmarks/quantderiv/<date>/
Regression detector flags changes with a false-positive rate < 5% on previously recorded stable baselines and triggers a Slack workflow with a bisect folder and suggested PR candidates.
p95 and p99 derivatives are computed per-interval and surfaced in Grafana with baseline overlay and automated anomaly annotations.
Harness supports cold-start, warmed-KV, and prefix-cached scenarios and documents the run config in CI metadata for reproducibility.
Playbook documented and reviewed by SRE and Applied ML teams (link in links).

implementation_notes: Metric model: compute tokens/sec over fixed 1s sliding windows, then estimate p50/p90/p95/p99 quantiles over a run using a 5-min rolling window. Fit a cubic spline on quantile time-series and compute first and second derivatives to detect changes in slope (derivative-of-quantile).
Baseline generation: use n=20 historical runs to build spline baseline and store coefficients in S3. Baseline update policy: rolling 30-day window with outlier exclusion (IQR gating).
Anomaly logic: flag run if (abs(derivative_diff) > k * baseline_std) for two or more quantiles among {p95,p99} OR if tokens/sec median drops >15% and p95 increases >20% concurrently.
Bisect output: produce a candidate report with run artifacts, representative request trace IDs, and a contended-resources score to help triage (GPU SM utilization, PCIe stall, host CPU steal).

Instrumentation: reuse existing microbench harness (bin/microbench) and extend with --trace-ids, --kv-warmup-seconds, and --emit-json-artifact flags. Artifacts must be gzipped JSON lines and include per-token timing samples up to 50k tokens/run.

Compute cluster: run canaries on dedicated cost-center machines (A100/H100) and a cheaper T4 baseline to catch regression-environment interactions. Use runner label mapping: canary: h100-prod-01, smoke: a100-stage-02.
Storage: artifacts to S3 and pointer in BigQuery table for long-term analysis. Dashboard panels read derived aggregates from BigQuery materialized view.
Rollbacks: integrate with Rollout service to automatically route a small fraction of traffic off suspect model variants while triage is in progress.
testing_plan: Unit tests for spline and derivative computations with synthetic signals (inference/runtime/bench/test_spline.py).
Replay tests: run harness in CI using stored request traces to validate deterministic tokens/sec under controlled concurrency and compare against baseline tolerance thresholds.
Canary smoke: daily low-concurrency canary with alert suppression window to validate pipeline and artifact ingestion.
Regression simulation: inject controlled latency into model containers and assert detector fires and bisect report is sufficient for root-cause.
Manual sign-off: run a full sweep across rw-3b, rw-7b, rw-13b-quantized on both H100 and A100 before enabling auto-alerts.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): land prototype flags and unit tests, run nightly smoke jobs without alerting; verify artifact ingestion and dashboard panels.
Phase 2 (week 2): enable canary daily and run full weekly sweep; iterate thresholds to meet <5% false positive target.
Phase 3 (week 3): enable automated Slack alerts with triage template and bisect artifact link; restrict auto-routing to experimental namespace.
Phase 4 (week 4): hand off playbook to SRE and Applied ML, add to runbooks and link in OnCall rotations.
risks: Noisy baselines due to infra variability could produce false positives; mitigation: require multi-quantile agreement and add host-level covariates into anomaly model.
Large artifact size could increase S3 costs; mitigation: sample token-level traces and keep full traces only for flagged runs.
Permission gap for scheduler SA to write to s3 bucket; mitigation: temporarily write to team bucket and escalate IAM ticket.
Detector complexity could make triage harder for oncall; mitigation: include clear bisect and contended-resource scoring in the generated report.
